title: Welsh Rarebit
subtitle: Savoury cheese sauce on toast
excerpt: The great British cheese on toast, improved into something much more interesting: a thick, glossy sauce of mature cheddar, beer, mustard, and Worcestershire sauce spread onto toast and grilled until blistered and bubbling. Sharp, savoury, and deeply satisfying.

recipe.sourceNotes: Welsh rarebit (historically also written as rabbit, though no rabbit is involved) has been eaten in Britain since at least the eighteenth century and is documented in recipe books from 1725. The dish is almost certainly Welsh in origin, reflecting the Welsh fondness for cheese dishes, though England also has a long tradition of melted cheese sauces. The defining technique is making the sauce: rather than simply melting cheese on toast, a thick sauce of cheese, beer (or ale), butter, mustard, and Worcestershire sauce is made, thickened with an egg yolk, and spread over toast before grilling. The result is a sauce that stays put on the toast, browns and blisters under the heat, and has a far more complex flavour than plain melted cheese. The use of strong ale adds bitterness and depth; English mustard (not French) gives the characteristic sharp heat.

content.text: Melt the cheese slowly into the sauce over very low heat; high heat can make it stringy and separate. The egg yolk thickens the sauce and makes it spread-able. Spread it generously: a thin coating will slide off the toast under the grill. The grill must be very hot so the sauce bubbles and chars in patches rather than just melting flatly.

items.preparation: thick slices; sourdough or a sturdy white bread; toasted
finely grated; use a very sharp, aged cheddar
or stout for a deeper flavour

content.text: Melt the butter in a small saucepan over low heat. Add the flour and stir for 1 minute. Add the ale and stir over medium heat until thickened and smooth, about 2 minutes. Remove from the heat.

Add the grated cheese, mustard, and Worcestershire sauce. Stir over low heat until the cheese has melted and the sauce is thick and smooth. Remove from the heat, leave to cool for 2 minutes, then stir in the egg yolk. Season with black pepper. The sauce should be thick enough to spread without running.

Heat the grill to its highest setting. Toast the bread. Spread the cheese sauce generously over each slice, all the way to the edges. Grill for 2 to 3 minutes until the sauce is bubbling and blistering in places. Serve immediately.
